title: Wych Elm: Old Elms You Can Visit
meta_description: The elm of northern Europe, cleared out by Dutch elm disease. On 12 May 1971 Stockholmers climbed into the Kungstradgarden elms and stopped the saws.
intro: On the night of 12 May 1971 a crowd of Stockholmers climbed into the elms of Kungstradgarden and refused to come down, and the city workers went home. Those trees are still standing, between 160 and 205 years old. Any wych elm of size is worth a detour now, because a fungus carried tree to tree by bark beetles cleared out most of the big ones within two generations. One of the oldest in the Netherlands, put at roughly 275 years, stands on a lawn behind an office building in The Hague that was a manor house first. Brighton's, in a dog exercise area above a playground, is the widest recorded in Sussex. Munich protects the elm on Maximiliansplatz precisely because almost every elm that size in the city has gone. Trento's stands in the garden facing the station, under two minutes from the platform.
